title.en: UK rapper Yung Filly found not guilty of raping woman after Australian show
title.zh: 英国说唱歌手Yung Filly在澳大利亚演出后被判强奸罪不成立

summary.en: UK YouTuber and rapper Yung Filly has been found not guilty of raping a woman following a show in Perth, Australia. However, he was found guilty of two counts of assault related to the same 2024 incident.
summary.zh: 英国YouTuber兼说唱歌手Yung Filly在澳大利亚珀斯演出后，被判强奸一名女性的罪名不成立。然而，他因与2024年同一事件相关的两项袭击罪名被判有罪。

body.en:
UK rapper Yung Filly has been found not guilty of raping a fan after performing at a nightclub in Australia in 2024.

On Friday a jury in Western Australia found him not guilty for three counts of sexual penetration without consent.

The YouTuber, whose real name is Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, had been accused of sexually assaulting the woman, then 20 years old, in his hotel room after he performed in Hillarys, a coastal suburb of Perth.

Barrientos was also found not guilty for one count of assault occasioning bodily harm and also for strangulation.

The 30-year-old social media star, who pleaded not guilty to all charges, cried when the verdict was read out, local media reported.

He will remain on bail until 21 August, when the court will decide his sentencing date.

Prosecutors will also decide on the next steps for the three hung jury verdicts - whether to press ahead or not on those rape charges.

Barrientos has been on bail since being charged and was allowed to fly home to the UK in September for four months, before returning to Western Australia ahead of his trial.

During the trial, Barrientos had told the court that he had "fancied" the woman when they met at the concert venue.

Barrientos, who was born in Colombia and brought up in the UK, had been in the VIP area while she leaned over the barrier from the general area.

"I recall putting my hand on her waist," he told the court. But he said he had not put his hands down her pants or touched her breast.

He said the "vibes were good" between him and the woman when they arrived at his hotel later.

His security guard took the woman's phone away - "standard practice" to protect their privacy, according to Barrientos.

The court heard that the pair had engaged in consensual sex in his hotel room before Barrientos turned violent and the young woman, who cannot be named for legal reasons, told him to stop.

The woman accused the social media star of biting, bruising and even trying to choke her. Photos of bruises and bite marks on her face and neck were shown in court.

Barrientos denied the woman had repeatedly asked him to stop, but did acknowledge that he bit her several times, explaining that he gave her a "love bite".

During the trial's closing arguments, prosecutor Danielle Clarke said Barrientos was an "entitled" man with a "moderate degree of fame" who had violated the fan "in the most intrusive way possible".

His defence lawyer argued that the accuser's evidence was full of "inconsistencies, embellishments and outright lies".

Barrientos is known for his work with the YouTube collective Beta Squad, and has appeared in the celebrity version of Bake Off on Channel 4 and presented BBC Three shows.

title.en: What could happen to Fifa if Uefa boycotts World Cup?
title.zh: 如果欧足联抵制世界杯，国际足联会发生什么？

summary.en: It's been a seismic 48 hours for football after Uefa threatened to boycott the World Cup and Concacaf rejected Gianni Infantino's funding plan - what happens now, and can Fifa's president survive?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In terms of impact, European football's governing body Uefa could not have gone any bigger.

"Uefa and its national associations will not participate in Fifa competitions," it said.

Eleven brutal words. The definitive reaction to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell a 20% stake in a subsidiary company set up to run the world governing body's competitions, including the World Cup.

A company it is intended Fifa will run but that will be part-funded by private investors, including the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Joshua Kushner.

It feels as though no-one who matters knows how this situation is going to play out just yet.

"Not sure the detail was considered when deciding the overall policy," was the response from a senior European football source when asked what this decision means for the U20 Women's World Cup, starting on 5 September, being hosted by Poland and featuring plenty of European nations.

Uefa's boycott threat will be activated if Infantino's funding deal is accepted.

Given 19 September is the deadline for countries to accept Fifa's deal and bank $20m (£15m) on 1 January, in theory, countries could be pulling out of that tournament in the middle of the quarter-finals and before the semis.

After that, the next senior matches in a Fifa competition are the Women's World Cup play-offs in October, which feature England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland among others.

"Wales is involved in the play-offs for the Women's World Cup in the autumn, and it would be our first qualification for a World Cup," Uefa vice-president and ex-Wales international Laura McAllister told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"But let's be clear here. This is not a problem of Uefa's making. It's a problem that Fifa have created. Nobody wants the players to suffer, and nobody wants nations to suffer when it comes to the most prestigious competitions.

No-one can be certain what happens now. And no-one knows what the future for Infantino is.

Uefa's statement was followed up by another from Concacaf, which governs football in North and Central America and hosted this year's World Cup, saying their 41 members rejected the proposals.

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt is a Fifa vice-president. She spoke out against the plan at Uefa's emergency meeting on Thursday. The FA said it stands "shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues" on the matter.

Scottish FA president Mike Mulraney is also chair of Fifa's finance committee. The Scottish FA's statement said the organisation "agrees unequivocally" with Uefa's stance.

The repeated responses from those who have spoken out are of fury at the lack of proper consultation and lack of dialogue from Infantino, including with his Fifa colleagues, as much as with the proposals...

body.en: Pre-programmed flights gather data at different altitudes then return to bases to recharge and download Weather happens in the boundary layer, the atmosphere from ground level to a few thousand metres, but this can be difficult to study in detail: weather stations are too low, and aircraft are expensive. Instrumented weather balloons are the traditional solution, and thousands are released every day. But these are at the mercy of the wind and use irreplaceable helium. Drones offer an alternative and the US company Meteomatics has taken the idea further with Meteobase , a base station on the ground with a drone that can be launched and recovered automatically. title.en: Anthropic says Claude AI hacked three organisations during cyber tests
title.zh: Anthropic称其人工智能模型在网络测试中攻破三家公司

summary.en: Anthropic reported that its AI models successfully hacked three companies during cybersecurity tests, following a similar disclosure from OpenAI about its AI agents breaching other networks.
summary.zh: Anthropic公司表示，其人工智能模型在网络安全测试中成功入侵了三家公司，此前其竞争对手OpenAI也曾透露其人工智能代理攻破了其他公司的网络。

body.en:
US technology firm Anthropic says its artificial intelligence (AI) models hacked into the systems of three organisations during a cybersecurity test due to an error that gave them access to the internet.

It comes just days after rival OpenAI said that its models had breached the systems of other companies , including AI tools hub Hugging Face.

The announcement prompted Anthropic to check whether its own models had carried out similar attacks. It says it uncovered three cases that have since been reported to the affected companies.

Anthropic, which did not name the organisations, urged other AI labs to perform similar reviews to better understand the risks of their models' capabilities.

Anthropic said in a statement , external that it reviewed more than 140,000 tests to find evidence that Claude - its family of AI models - could access the internet from testing environments that were designed to be sealed off.

The tests include so-called "capture-the-flag" evaluations in which Claude was tasked with obtaining information by breaching other systems - a common way that experts assess a model's hacking capabilities.

A "misconfiguration" on systems run by Anthropic and its testing partner left the models with live internet access, allowing them to breach other systems, the San Francisco-based firm said.

Anthropic said the earliest incidents date back to April and that it is "approaching the fixes as if the responsibility were ours alone."

Neither Anthropic nor the organisations that were breached had noticed the intrusions at the time.

Anthropic said it could have reviewed its records more thoroughly and added that the findings gave the firm "cautious optimism" that such risks can be overcome with more investment and tighter measures.

"The broader lesson is not necessarily that AI has developed a fundamentally new attack capability," cyber security expert David Allott told the BBC.

"Instead, it is that AI agents can combine capabilities, obtain credentials and system access to take actions autonomously, while adapting scope and scale at machine speed," he added.

The incidents come as tech firms pour billions of dollars into developing AI agents that can independently perform tasks ranging from research and customer support to cybersecurity.

A string of AI-driven cyberattacks has fuelled calls for tighter safeguards and oversight of the technology, over concerns about the risks posed by increasingly powerful autonomous systems.

US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that Washington is considering measures to rein in AI tools after recent cybersecurity incidents.

Over the last week, OpenAI has taken responsibility for at least two hacking incidents involving its platforms breaching the rules of what they were directed to do.

title.en: Rushdi Abualouf: If Hamas disarmament plan holds, it could mark first credible step to ending Gaza war
title.zh: 拉什迪·阿布卢夫：如果哈马斯解除武装计划成功，这可能标志着结束加沙战争的第一步

summary.en: The plan - if successful - potentially removes the most significant obstacle to advancing the Trump-backed peace initiative in Gaza.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
After months of marathon talks, Hamas has, for the first time, accepted a framework of the Board of Peace's plan to completely disarm in Gaza.

The plan provides for the inventorying and storage of its remaining heavy weapons under Palestinian supervision, potentially removing the most significant obstacle to advancing the Trump-backed peace initiative for Gaza.

The move comes soon after Hamas concluded leadership elections that brought Gaza-based leader Khalil al-Hayya to the head of the movement .

Palestinian officials involved in the talks believe the new leadership was prepared to take what they describe as the most consequential political decision in Hamas's history, driven by the devastating humanitarian conditions facing more than two million Palestinians in Gaza.

A senior Hamas official and member of the movement's negotiating team told the BBC that the talks were "long and extremely difficult", with Hamas insisting on the wording "inventorying and storing weapons" under Palestinian oversight rather than handing them over to Israel.

It remains too early to judge whether the agreement will be fully implemented or whether all parties will honour their commitments.

But if it holds, it could mark the first credible step towards ending a war that has lasted for nearly three years and opening the way for a broader political process.

After years of failed ceasefires and collapsed agreements, many Palestinians have grown deeply sceptical of new political breakthroughs.

Some residents shared their views online, saying they are less interested in the details of negotiations than in whether this deal will actually end the war, allow displaced families to return home and bring lasting relief.

For many, confidence in both Hamas and Israel remains low, with previous agreements having repeatedly broken down before delivering meaningful improvements on the ground.
body.zh: 经过数月的马拉松式谈判，哈马斯首次接受了和平委员会全面解除加沙武装计划的框架。 该计划规定在巴勒斯坦的监督下库存和储存剩余的重型武器，这有可能消除推进特朗普支持的加沙和平倡议的最大障碍。 此举是在哈马斯结束领导人选举后不久做出的，选举使加沙领导人哈利勒·哈亚成为该运动的领导人。 参与谈判的巴勒斯坦官员相信，新领导层准备做出他们所说的哈马斯历史上最重要的政治决定，原因是加沙超过两百万巴勒斯坦人面临着毁灭性的人道主义状况。 哈马斯的一名高级官员和该运动谈判小组的成员告诉英国广播公司，谈判“漫长且极其困难”，哈马斯坚持在巴勒斯坦监督下“清查和储存武器”，而不是将其交给以色列。 现在判断协议是否全面执行、各方是否履行承诺还为时过早。 但如果它成立，这可能标志着结束一场持续近三年的战争并为更广泛的政治进程开辟道路的第一步。 经过多年的停火失败和协议破裂，许多巴勒斯坦人对新的政治突破深感怀疑。 一些居民在网上分享了他们的看法，称他们对谈判细节不太感兴趣，而更关心这项协议是否能真正结束战争、让流离失所的家庭返回家园并带来持久的救济。 对于许多人来说，对哈马斯和以色列的信心仍然很低，之前的协议在实地取得有意义的改善之前就一再破裂。

title.en: Fifa says 'nobody selling football' as it presses ahead with investment plan
title.zh: 国际足联在推进投资计划时表示“没有人出售足球”

summary.en: Football's governing body plans to continue the consultation process after Uefa threatens to boycott World Cups.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Fifa, which oversees world football, has responded to outrage over a plan to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors by saying it plans to continue the consultation process.

European football's 55 member associations (MAs) voted on Thursday to boycott World Cups if Fifa proceeded with the proposal.

And Concacaf, which governs football in North and Central America, said its 41 member associations also "rejected" the plan.

Fifa said in response: "⁠Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.

Fifa wants to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, and external investors will be able to buy stakes in it.

It said it would "invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments" in a new subsidiary - Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

Infantino needs 106 votes in favour for the proposal to go through. Uefa and Concacaf members combined make up 96 associations, who appear set to vote against.

In its statement released on Friday morning, Fifa said: "We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation."

The statement continued: "FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself."
body.zh: 负责监督世界足球的国际足联回应了一项向私人投资者出售其赛事股份的计划的愤怒，表示计划继续进行磋商过程。 周四，欧洲足球 55 个成员协会 (MA) 投票决定，如果国际足联继续执行该提案，将抵制世界杯。 管理北美和中美洲足球的中北美及加勒比地区足联表示，其 41 个成员协会也“拒绝”了该计划。 国际足联回应称：“我们原定的磋商过程因媒体错误报道而中断。我们将继续进行这一磋商过程，以确保每个MA都有能力根据事实表达自己的投票。” 国际足联希望成立一家商业子公司来运营包括世界杯在内的主要赛事，外部投资者将能够购买其股份。 该公司表示，将“邀请第三方对新子公司 Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) 进行少数股权、非控股投资”。 因凡蒂诺需要 106 票赞成才能通过该提案。欧足联和中北美及加勒比地区足联成员共有 96 个协会，这些协会似乎将投反对票。 国际足联在周五上午发布的声明中表示：“我们尊重公开表达的反馈和担忧，并重申我们对公开和民主协商的承诺。” 声明继续说道：“提出FFE只是为了确保所有国际足联会员协会（MA）都有机会在各自国家获得对足球商业机会的有意义的所有权，并且这不会以牺牲国际足联或足球本身的精神或治理为代价。”

title.en: The Spanish territory at the centre of a unique migration challenge
title.zh: 数百名移民从摩洛哥进入休达飞地，西班牙调动武装部队

summary.en: Spanish authorities deployed armed forces to the Ceuta exclave after hundreds of migrants entered the territory from Morocco. This incident highlights the long-standing and politically sensitive issue of migration between the two nations, which has now escalated into a flashpoint.
summary.zh: 数百名移民从摩洛哥进入西班牙飞地休达后，西班牙当局调动了武装部队。这一事件凸显了摩洛哥和西班牙之间长期存在的政治敏感移民问题，该问题现已升级为冲突爆发点。

body.en:
Madrid says it will dispatch soldiers to Ceuta to ensure security after hundreds of migrants entered Spain's North African exclave from neighbouring Morocco and hundreds more headed there.

The Spanish government's delegation in the exclave told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency on Friday that the bodies of nine migrants who died while trying to reach Ceuta by swimming the previous day had been recovered.

Migration from Morocco into Spain's two north African territories, Ceuta and Melilla, has long been a politically sensitive issue between the two countries, as thousands cross the border at times.

On Friday, Italy called for Spain to be suspended from Europe's open-borders Schengen zone, prompting a backlash from Spain, which summoned the Italian envoy to Madrid.

AFP reporters saw a stream of adults and children, most of them soaked, entering the town of Ceuta after having swum there. Discarded flotation rings and clothes were left on the shore near where the border barrier meets the sea.

"The armed forces will reinforce the Civil Guard in the exercise of its powers and any others that may be necessary to maintain security in the city of Ceuta," Spain's interior ministry said.

It did not specify how many soldiers would be sent to the small territory of 18.5 square kilometres but said the Civil Guard's strength there would be nearly doubled from the current level of 80.

Though Morocco and Spain face each other across the narrow Strait of Gibraltar, the Spanish city of Ceuta actually lies on the Moroccan side of the waterway.

Ceuta is an autonomous city, one of a series of small Spanish outposts along the Moroccan coastline. These cities are referred to as "plazas de soberanía" or "strongholds of sovereignty". Like its sister city Melilla, Ceuta is a popular target for African migrants hoping to gain entry to Europe.

Ceuta is fenced off and heavily policed to prevent Moroccan migrants arriving over land, but it does have a port and a beach. Thus, the fastest option for a migrant looking to make it into Spanish territory is to swim from a neighbouring town, follow the Moroccan coastline and approach Ceuta by water.

Because Morocco doesn't recognise Spanish sovereignty in Ceuta, and strongly opposed the construction of the fence around the city in the first place, Spain faces waves of migrants with little local assistance.

United States President Donald Trump has announced an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas, calling it a critical step toward a new Palestinian government in Gaza.

Specific details about what the deal will look like are slim, with neither Israel nor Hamas releasing public statements following Trump's announcement.

"Today, the Board of Peace reached a HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza. This is a monumental step toward lasting PEACE and SECURITY," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform on Friday, saying disarmament would take place in phases.

"At the same time, Israel will have the security it deserves, with Gaza no longer used as a base for terror attacks."

He said it was a "major milestone in the implementation of the Trump 20-Point Plan" and said it would be carried out in "carefully structured phases".

"One year ago there was a violent raging war, humanitarian crisis and hostages kept in brutal captivity. We have made historic progress and there is still much work to do.

"The threat that emerged from Gaza on October 7 will NOT be allowed to rebuild!"

"Under this agreement, Gaza will finally be in the hands of a new Palestinian government that serves its PEOPLE.

"CONGRATULATIONS TO ALL ON THIS AMAZING DEVELOPMENT, THAT EVERYBODY SAID COULD NEVER BE ACHIEVED!"

Specific details of the deal are not yet public, with a full breakdown expected to be released within two weeks.

Hamas officials have reportedly agreed to the deal, though they have not yet made a public statement.

An anonymous Hamas official told news wire Agence France-Presse (AFP) the roadmap offered a "balanced and pragmatic path forward, with all weapons decommissioned".

The source added there would be a "phased transition of responsibilities taking place to hand over full authority to the technocratic government".

They added there would be "no exceptions" for weapons or people, with all tunnels, weapons depots and production facilities to be eliminated and full control passing to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, working alongside the International Stabilisation Force.

body.en:
Mediator Pakistan insisted on Friday that negotiations between Iran and the United States were ongoing, even as the US carried out a "heavy wave of strikes" on its foe in retaliation for fresh attacks targeting Jordan.

The last two days have seen Saudi Arabia join the US in striking militant groups in Iraq and Egypt come under fire for the first time with a drone attack at a Mediterranean port, leading its president to warn that the Middle East conflict is facing a serious escalation.

On Thursday, Jordan reported intercepting Iranian missiles for a second day running, while Kuwait said an Iranian strike that hit a building belonging to a Chinese company killed one person.

The return to direct hostilities followed a brief pause in fighting meant to give talks a boost.

"Negotiations between parties are ongoing, particularly on (the) Strait of Hormuz and to de-escalate," Pakistani foreign ministry spokesman Tahir Andrabi told reporters.

Pakistan had helped to broker a deal between the warring sides laying the groundwork for negotiations on a permanent resolution, and Andrabi said it was doing its "utmost to bring all parties back" to technical talks under the agreement.

Previous talks following an April truce stalled, with the ceasefire collapsing earlier this month and Iran again slamming shut the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for oil and gas.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Thursday that two oil tankers attempting to transit the strait with US support turned back after one of them caught fire.

Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, said it had set up a maritime defence alliance of 14 regional countries to secure navigation around the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.

The move comes after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said last week they were imposing a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia and claimed attacks targeting Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea.

The narrow maritime artery has been a critical waterway for delivering vast quantities of Saudi crude to the international market, after energy exports were choked off by the US-Iran standoff in the Strait of Hormuz.

Earlier, the US military said it had "successfully completed a heavy wave of strikes against Iran", hitting dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets including military command centres.

US President Donald Trump had vowed to hit Iran "hard" after Iran's previous attack on Jordan, its first in the region in days.

The Guards' branch in the northwestern province of Zanjan said three of its members were killed in a US attack there.

body.en:
European football's governing body UEFA has said it would boycott the World Cup if FIFA pressed ahead with a controversial private investor plan.

"No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership," UEFA said in a statement released on Friday.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product ... No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale."

On Tuesday, football's world governing body FIFA announced plans to create a commercial subsidiary to run its biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

Under the proposal, private investors would be allowed to acquire stakes in the company but would remain minority shareholders, FIFA said.

It hopes to raise up to US$4.2 billion ($5.9 billion) based on a valuation of US$20 billion ($28 billion) for the FIFA Forward Enterprise initiative.

If approved, the project could provide each of FIFA's 211 member associations with a one-off payment of $20 million in early 2027 and increase their funding allocation for the 2027-2030 cycle from $8 million ($11.3 million) to US$20 million ($28 million).

FIFA president Gianni Infantino described the initiative on Wednesday as a "golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally".

But UEFA, whose president Aleksander Čeferin boycotted the World Cup final to show unhappiness with FIFA, argued: "This model has no place in world football.

"Football's future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return.

"Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain," Čeferin said.

"Europe's position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No-one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation."

title.en: Are Iran and Ukraine wars getting tangled in Caspian Sea?
title.zh: 伊朗和乌克兰的战争是否正在里海纠缠不清？

summary.en: Tehran has issued a threat of retaliation following a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea, which Kyiv claims was transporting weapons to Russia. Despite this, Ukraine has expressed its intention to prevent further escalation with Tehran.
summary.zh: 德黑兰威胁要对乌克兰在里海袭击一艘伊朗货船进行报复，基辅称该货船向俄罗斯运送武器。尽管如此，乌克兰表示希望避免与德黑兰的局势升级。

body.en:
Tehran has threatened a response after a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea that Kyiv says was carrying weapons to Russia. Still, Ukraine says it wants to avoid escalation with Tehran.

A recent Ukrainian strike on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea has drawn concerns that Russia's war in Ukraine  and the war in Iran are becoming entangled.

Ukraine has said the ship was carrying military equipment from Iran to Russia. Iranian state media, citing Iran's ambassador to Russia, Kazem Jalali, reported that the cargo vessel "Anna" was anchored approximately 5 kilometers (3 miles) from the entrance of the Volga River when it was attacked by drones causing an explosion. One sailor was reported killed.

Iran summoned Ukraine's charge d'affaires and described the incident as an act of aggression.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, meanwhile, said Ukrainian forces had carried out successful long-range strikes against a Russian warship and vessels that Kyiv says were transporting military cargo.

Ukraine has long accused Iran of helping Russia wage war through the supply and development of Iranian-designed drones.

Tehran has acknowledged earlier drone sales to Moscow but has rejected accusations that it supplied weapons specifically for use in the Ukraine war.

However, the Ukrainian military has extensive documented physical evidence that Iranian-designed Shahed drones have been deployed throughout the war that has dragged on for more than four years.

In March 2026, Russia launched nearly 950 Shahed, Gerber and other types of attack drones at Ukraine in a 24-hour period, according to Ukraine's Air Force.

Iran's Foreign Ministry has accused Ukraine of attempting to expand the geographical scope of its war with Russia. Kyiv, by contrast, presents its attacks in the Caspian Sea as part of an effort to disrupt military logistics supporting Moscow.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a statement the attack "cannot go unanswered."

However, Ahmad Vakhshiteh, director of the Moscow-based Center for Strategic Research on Developing Relations with the Middle East, told DW that Tehran is unlikely to respond immediately with a direct military strike against Ukraine.

"I believe the Islamic Republic will avoid an emotional reaction and choose a diplomatic response instead of a military one," he said, pointing to Tehran's summoning of the Ukrainian diplomat and the possibility of raising the matter at the UN Security Council.

On Monday, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha posted on X that Iran's accusations were "unjustified and groundless."

body.zh: 乌克兰在里海袭击了一艘伊朗货船，基辅称这艘货船当时正在向俄罗斯运送武器，德黑兰威胁要做出回应。尽管如此，乌克兰表示希望避免与德黑兰的冲突升级。 最近乌克兰在里海袭击了一艘伊朗船只，引发了人们的担忧，即俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争和伊朗的战争正在变得纠缠在一起。 乌克兰表示，这艘船正在从伊朗向俄罗斯运送军事装备。伊朗官方媒体援引伊朗驻俄罗斯大使卡齐姆·贾拉利的话报道称，货船“安娜”号停泊在距伏尔加河入口约 5 公里（3 英里）处，遭到无人机袭击并引发爆炸。据报道，一名水手被杀。 伊朗召见乌克兰临时代办，并将该事件描述为侵略行为。 与此同时，乌克兰总统泽伦斯基表示，乌克兰军队对一艘俄罗斯军舰和基辅称正在运输军事货物的船只进行了成功的远程打击。 乌克兰长期以来一直指责伊朗通过供应和开发伊朗设计的无人机来帮助俄罗斯发动战争。 德黑兰承认早些时候曾向莫斯科出售无人机，但否认其专门为乌克兰战争提供武器的指控。 然而，乌克兰军方拥有大量有据可查的物证，表明伊朗设计的“沙赫德”无人机在这场持续了四年多的战争中得到了部署。 据乌克兰空军称，2026年3月，俄罗斯在24小时内向乌克兰发射了近950架“沙赫德”、“格伯”和其他类型的攻击无人机。 伊朗外交部指责乌克兰试图扩大与俄罗斯战争的地理范围。相比之下，基辅将其在里海的袭击视为破坏支持莫斯科的军事后勤努力的一部分。 伊朗外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇在一份声明中表示，这次袭击“不能不予回应”。 然而，总部位于莫斯科的中东关系战略研究中心主任艾哈迈德·瓦赫希特（Ahmad Vakhshiteh）告诉德国之声，德黑兰不太可能立即对乌克兰进行直接军事打击。 他说：“我相信伊斯兰共和国将避免情绪化反应，选择外交回应，而不是军事回应。”他指的是德黑兰召见乌克兰外交官以及向联合国安理会提出此事的可能性。 周一，乌克兰外交部长安德里·西比哈 (Andrii Sybiha) 在 X 上发帖称，伊朗的指控“毫无道理且毫无根据”。 “德黑兰政权是俄罗斯侵略乌克兰的直接帮凶，用武器助长了莫斯科的罪恶战争，导致……

title.en: Epstein files: How victims remain exposed to identification
title.zh: 爱泼斯坦档案：受害者如何继续暴露身份

summary.en: US officials vowed to revise redactions after files exposed information that identified survivors of sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. A DW investigation found that sensitive information remains online.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 在文件曝光了杰弗里·爱泼斯坦及其同伙性虐待幸存者的信息后，美国官员发誓要修改修订内容。德国之声的一项调查发现敏感信息仍然在线。 一名性虐待幸存者在 5 月份对美国立法者表示：“如果不警惕，我就无法生活。”她描述了 1 月份她的个人信息如何被公开曝光的情况，当时司法部 (DOJ) 公布了数十万份与金融家杰弗里·爱泼斯坦 (Jeffrey Epstein) 有关的文件。 “我只能想象这个错误将对我的生活产生的长期影响。” 1 月 30 日，司法部公布了有关爱泼斯坦的 12 个数据集中最大的一个，三天后，一名部门律师告诉联邦法院，“人为或技术错误”是导致被爱泼斯坦及其同伙性虐待的人的个人识别信息被公开的因素之一。因此，司法部表示将在重新发布之前删除、审查和编辑标记的文件。 德国之声的调查部门及其创新和数据团队花了几个月的时间审查了司法部发布的数千份文件。在发布后的六个月内，德国之声发现了数十个文件，其中仍然包含信息，包括姓名、面孔和电子邮件地址，这些信息可用于识别幸存者、目击者和线人等人的身份。 到 2 月中旬，德国之声已从 DOJ 的 Epstein 图书馆中删除了超过 800,000 个文件，这是一项艰巨的任务，因为档案不断变化：新文件被添加，其他文件被删除，修改后的文件在消失几天后又出现。 但直到 DW 获得了 GitHub 上一个面向公众的数据保存项目存档的一组早期文件，我们才意识到在发布的最初几天和我们的抓取之间有超过 500,000 个文件被删除。 为了验证原始版本的内容，DW 为每个文档生成了一个唯一的数字指纹，称为哈希值。哈希值确认文档与原始文档匹配且未被更改。通过将这些指纹与大约两周后从 DOJ 网站上抓取的文件进行比较，德国之声可以确定哪些文件匹配，并识别已从 DOJ 网站上删除的文件。 德国之声还发现，一些文件发生了变化，因为数字指纹不再相同：它们具有相同的文件名，但比原始文件更大或更小。当德国之声审查这个子集时，我们发现它们代表了经过进一步编辑的文件，或者添加了信息。 有一次，一名幸存者在向律师作证时描述了爱泼斯坦在她未成年时如何虐待她多年。

title.en: Human trafficking in Mexico: the dark side of tourism
title.zh: 墨西哥的人口贩卖：旅游业的阴暗面

summary.en: By May, a record-breaking 20 million tourists had visited Mexico so far in 2026. But with increased tourism comes a heightened risk of human trafficking and sexual exploitation. Women and children are most vulnerable.

title.en: The future of AI hinges on openness and cooperation. China and Britain can gain much by working together | Zheng Zeguang
title.zh: 人工智能的未来取决于开放与合作。中英携手合作，收获良多 |郑泽光

summary.en: There is no point competing in isolation. There are so many benefits to be had, in manufacturing, healthcare, research and governance Zheng Zeguang is the Chinese ambassador to the UK Artificial intelligence is widely regarded as one of the defining technologies of our time....
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: There is no point competing in isolation. There are so many benefits to be had, in manufacturing, healthcare, research and governance Zheng Zeguang is the Chinese ambassador to the UK Artificial intelligence is widely regarded as one of the defining technologies of our time. Like the steam engine, the harnessing of electricity and the internet before it, it has the potential to transform how we work, live and interact. But every technological revolution brings challenges as well as opportunities. As AI systems become more capable, people are asking legitimate questions. How can AI remain safe, accountable and under human control ? How should its development be governed? How can its benefits be shared more widely? Continue reading...
body.zh: 孤立地竞争是没有意义的。在制造、医疗保健、研究和治理方面有很多好处。郑泽光是中国驻英国大使人工智能被广泛认为是我们这个时代的决定性技术之一。就像蒸汽机、电力和互联网的利​​用一样，它有可能改变我们的工作、生活和互动方式。但每一次技术革命都带来挑战和机遇。随着人工智能系统变得越来越强大，人们提出了合理的问题。人工智能如何保持安全、负责任并处于人类控制之下？其发展又该如何治理？如何让更广泛的人分享其好处？继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to hope, endurance, and faithful rebuilding. Romans 12:12 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with steady hope and perseverance, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到盼望、忍耐与重建。Romans 12:12提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以坚定盼望与忍耐来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
verse.textZh: 就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。

title.en: Anthony Fauci’s diaries take aim at News Corp journalist Sharri Markson’s ‘nonsense’ Covid-19 investigation
title.zh: 安东尼·福奇日记抨击新闻集团记者沙里·马克森的“胡说八道”新冠疫情调查

body.en: US former top health official, who was subpoenaed to appear at a Senate hearing into Covid-19, says Markson’s reporting about virus’s origin ‘does not make any sense’ Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Dr Anthony Fauci , the US’s chief medical adviser at the start of the pandemic, has described a book by News Corp investigative journalist Sharri Markson backing the “lab leak” theory of Covid-19’s origins as a “bunch of nonsense” in his newly released diaries. This week, Fauci, 85, was subpoenaed by the Republican senator Rand Paul to appear at a Senate hearing into Covid-19 and his handling of the pandemic. Continue reading...

reflection.en: In public discourse, especially when complex issues like a pandemic's origins are debated, it is wise to consider all perspectives. As Proverbs 18:17 reminds us, the first account often seems right until another view is presented and examined. This encourages us to seek understanding from various sources before forming conclusions.
reflection.zh: 在公共讨论中，尤其当涉及疫情起源等复杂议题时，倾听各方观点是明智之举。正如箴言18:17提醒我们，先陈述案情的人似乎有理，直到另一方前来查问。这鼓励我们在下结论之前，从不同来源寻求理解。

title.en: The Chinese robot army transforming the UK's retail industry
title.zh: 改变英国零售业的中国机器人大军

summary.en: Britain's retail sector is increasingly adopting robotics from Chinese firms to combat low productivity and labor shortages.
summary.zh: 英国零售业正日益采用中国机器人公司的技术，以应对生产力低下和劳动力短缺的问题。

body.en:
Every time you click "buy" on an online order, the chances are that your purchase starts getting processed within minutes.

Increasingly, the journey starts with a squat silver floor robot gliding beneath a storage rack, lifting a shelf and carrying it across a warehouse to a waiting worker.

At Geek+'s factory in the eastern Chinese city of Hefei, which the BBC visited, fleets of the robots are built and tested before being shipped to warehouses around the world.

Some of Britain's biggest retailers - including Tesco, Asda and Next - now use the company's technology.

By automating these repetitive journeys, Geek+ says retailers can increase picking speeds, store more goods in spaces that are hard to reach for humans, and reduce errors.

Unlike traditional warehouse automation, which relies on fixed conveyor systems and permanent infrastructure, autonomous mobile robots can be deployed simply using QR code floor markers and safety fencing.

Geek+, which listed in Hong Kong last year in one of the biggest robotics share sales of 2025, has become the world's largest supplier of autonomous mobile robots.

The UK has struggled with weak productivity growth for more than a decade, and economists say wider adoption of robotics will be essential if businesses are to become more efficient.

In its 2026 report SME Technology Adoption in the United Kingdom, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) said technologies like robotics would be key to improving productivity.

According to the OECD, Britain's low adoption of robotics is "surprising" given its manufacturing heritage, noting that while UK firms have embraced mature digital technologies, they lag behind in robotics and automation.

That presents an opportunity for companies such as Geek+. The UK has one of Europe's largest e-commerce and logistics sectors, but many warehouses are still in the early stages of automation.

Britain has already become Geek+'s biggest European market, with UK partner MotionTech deploying more than 2,000 robots across 10 warehouse sites.

"Customers want fast deployable solutions," says Barry Pemberton, Account Director at MotionTech. "They want high volume, high storage, fast picking... ultimately on a smaller footprint with a reduced headcount."

"We seem to have a very big shortage of labour in the UK at the moment. These technologies are really important to keep businesses thriving and meet demand."

The Trades Union Congress (TUC), which represents almost 6 million UK workers, says robotics should be used to raise productivity and improve jobs, rather than simply cut labour costs.

In its response to the government's consultation on a new AI and innovation strategy, it urged ministers to ensure workers are involved in decisions about automation...
body.zh: 每次您在在线订单上点击“购买”时，您的购买很可能会在几分钟内开始处理。 越来越多的旅程开始于一个矮胖的银色地板机器人在存储架下滑行，举起一个架子并将其穿过仓库交给等待的工人。 BBC 参观了 Geek+ 位于中国东部城市合肥的工厂，机器人车队在被运往世界各地的仓库之前进行了建造和测试。 英国一些最大的零售商——包括Tesco、Asda和Next——现在都在使用该公司的技术。 Geek+ 表示，通过自动化这些重复的旅程，零售商可以提高拣选速度，在人类难以到达的空间中存储更多商品，并减少错误。 与依赖固定输送系统和永久性基础设施的传统仓库自动化不同，自主移动机器人只需使用二维码地板标记和安全围栏即可部署。 Geek+去年在香港上市，成为2025年机器人股销量最大的公司之一，现已成为全球最大的自主移动机器人供应商。 十多年来，英国一直在与生产率增长疲软作斗争，经济学家表示，如果企业要提高效率，更广泛地采用机器人技术至关重要。 经济合作与发展组织 (OECD) 在其 2026 年英国中小企业技术采用报告中表示，机器人等技术将是提高生产力的关键。 经合组织表示，鉴于其制造业传统，英国机器人技术的采用率较低“令人惊讶”，并指出虽然英国公司已经采用了成熟的数字技术，但它们在机器人技术和自动化方面仍然落后。 这为 Geek+ 等公司提供了机会。英国拥有欧洲最大的电子商务和物流行业之一，但许多仓库仍处于自动化的早期阶段。 英国已经成为 Geek+ 最大的欧洲市场，英国合作伙伴 MotionTech 在 10 个仓库站点部署了 2000 多台机器人。 “客户需要快速部署的解决方案，”MotionTech 客户总监 Barry Pemberton 说道。 “他们想要高产量、高存储量、快速拣选……最终以更小的占地面积和更少的人员数量。” “目前英国的劳动力似乎非常短缺。这些技术对于保持企业繁荣和满足需求非常重要。” 代表近 600 万英国工人的工会大会 (TUC) 表示，机器人技术应该用于提高生产力和改善就业，而不是简单地削减劳动力成本。 在回应政府关于新的人工智能和创新战略的咨询时，它敦促部长们确保工人参与有关自动化的决策......

Colossians 3:23 reminds us to approach every task with diligence and integrity, working heartily as for Yahweh. title.en: US bans Chinese and foreign-made humanoid robots
title.zh: 美国禁止中国及外国制造的仿人机器人

summary.en: The Trump administration has prohibited the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. This ban could potentially escalate diplomatic tensions with China.
summary.zh: 特朗普政府以国家安全为由，禁止进口美国以外制造的仿人机器人和四足机器人。这项禁令可能会加剧与中国的外交紧张关系。

body.en:
The Trump administration has banned the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. The ban could strain diplomatic tensions with China.

The United States has announced a ban on the import of foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots in a move which will likely exclude Chinese manufacturers from the US market and could strain tensions between Washington and Beijing .

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Tuesday that "advanced robotic devices" produced abroad posed national and cyber security risks to the United States.

The decision was based on findings from a White House task force which concluded that foreign-built robots could create "a cybersecurity risk that threatens the security of critical infrastructure" and "the safety and security" of US residents.

The FCC defines the relevant mobile robots as devices weighing more than two kilograms that use sensors, network connectivity and software to achieve autonomous navigation, including the avoidance of obstacles.

The market for humanoid and quadruped (also known as four-legged "robot dogs") is seen as a major international growth area, with US and Chinese companies competing to develop the technology.

And China has a clear lead, with analysts at Barclays estimating that Chinese-made humanoid robots account for around 85% of the global market share. Morgan Stanley experts predict that China's humanoid robot market could be worth $15 billion (€13.2 billion) by 2030.

"Chinese manufacturers have been scaling production and reducing costs faster than most overseas competitors," Morningstar analyst Kangyuxiao Li told the Associated Press .

In the US, firms such as Figure AI are already deploying humanoid robots on production lines, while tech giant Tesla plans to begin production of its "Optimus" robot this year.

Currently, however, US robot exports remain in their hundreds while Unitree and AGIBOT, two of China's biggest advanced robotics companies, each shipped more than 5,000 humanoid robots in 2025 alone, according to the technology research and advisory group Omdia.

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the ban was also aimed at "secur[ing] America's critical supply chains."

But Li said the measures would not "materially slow China's overall humanoid development, given the size of its domestic manufacturing base and opportunities in other export markets."

Beyond the industrial market effects, the FCC ban could also have diplomatic consequences ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese Premier Xi Jinping in September.

body.zh: 特朗普政府以国家安全为由，禁止进口在美国境外制造的人形和四足机器人。该禁令可能会加剧与中国的外交紧张关系。 美国已宣布禁止进口外国制造的人形和四足机器人，此举可能会将中国制造商排除在美国市场之外，并可能加剧华盛顿和北京之间的紧张关系。 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）周二表示，国外生产的“先进机器人设备”对美国构成国家和网络安全风险。 该决定是基于白宫特别工作组的调查结果，该工作组得出的结论是，外国制造的机器人可能会造成“威胁关键基础设施安全的网络安全风险”和美国居民的“安全保障”。 FCC将相关移动机器人定义为重量超过两公斤、使用传感器、网络连接和软件实现自主导航，包括避开障碍物的设备。 人形和四足动物（也称为四足“机器狗”）市场被视为主要的国际增长领域，美国和中国公司竞相开发该技术。 中国明显领先，巴克莱分析师估计，中国制造的人形机器人约占全球市场份额的 85%。摩根士丹利专家预测，到 2030 年，中国的仿人机器人市场价值可能达到 150 亿美元（132 亿欧元）。 晨星公司分析师李康宇告诉美联社：“中国制造商扩大生产和降低成本的速度比大多数海外竞争对手更快。” 在美国，Figure AI 等公司已经在生产线上部署人形机器人，而科技巨头特斯拉计划今年开始生产其“Optimus”机器人。 然而，根据技术研究和咨询集团 Omdia 的数据，目前美国机器人出口量仍为数百台，而中国最大的两家先进机器人公司 Unitree 和 AGIBOT 仅在 2025 年就分别出货了 5,000 多台人形机器人。 FCC 主席布伦丹·卡尔表示，该禁令还旨在“保护美国关键供应链的安全”。 但李表示，鉴于其国内制造基地的规模和其他出口市场的机会，这些措施不会“实质性地减缓中国整体人形机器人的发展”。 除了工业市场影响之外，FCC 禁令还可能在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普与中国总理习近平 9 月会晤之前产生外交后果。 美国已经禁止进口中国制造的无人机，并正在考虑限制中国开源人工智能（AI）模型，理由是……

title.en: Where Australia sits in this $6 billion race for influence as China's strategy shifts
title.zh: 澳大利亚在这场60亿美元的影响力竞争中处于何种位置，中国战略正在转变

summary.en: A new report indicates that China's strategic influence in the Pacific region, which was once significant, has recently diminished. This shift is noted amidst a broader competition for influence involving countries like Australia.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，中国在太平洋地区曾拥有的“真正立足点”已有所缩小。这一变化是在澳大利亚等国更广泛的地区影响力竞争中被观察到的。

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

body.en:
Every five years, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) counts every person and every household in the country as part of the Census of Population and Housing .

That includes Australians, young and old, from metropolitan and rural Australia. Even holidaymakers, international students and temporary visa holders are counted. It's often referred to as the most comprehensive snapshot of Australia, akin to a family photograph of the country.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

From late July, households will receive instructions on how to complete the Census. Australians can complete the form as soon as they receive instructions, provided they know where they will be on Census night.

Most people will receive a letter with instructions to complete the Census online. However, Australians can also request a paper form if they prefer.

Generally, one person per household will complete the Census, but separate forms can be requested for privacy reasons.

Census data is used to inform decisions about language services, settlement support, transport, schools, health care, infrastructure and business. It also helps plan local services for individuals, families and communities.

SBS broadcasts and publishes across more than 60 languages, using data from the Census to ensure its audio, digital, and television offerings reflect the country's evolving demographics.

The data is often used by researchers to study a range of topics, including population demographics, economic trends and social issues.

International visitors, migrants, refugees and people on temporary visas (including international students and tourists) must also complete the Census.

People staying in hotels, motels, or bed and breakfasts can access paper Census forms from accommodation staff. Those staying in short-term rental accommodation (like an Airbnb or Stayz) can complete the Census online with internet access.

The Census is strictly confidential. Personal information such as names and addresses cannot be accessed by police, immigration agents or any government departments.

For international visitors and students staying in hotels, motels or student accommodation, instructions on how to complete the Census will be provided by accommodation staff.

Paper forms should be available at locations including bed and breakfasts, cruise ships, commercial vessels and snowfield accommodation.

body.en:
Victoria has the sorry distinction of being the national capital for court-imposed gag orders.

The courts and tribunals of that state issue more than half the tally of suppressions for all the other states and territories combined.

A count of these orders is religiously kept by Gina McWilliams, a senior legal counsel at News Corp. Her tally for 2025 totalled 1,226 suppression and no-publication orders Australia-wide.

Victoria, including the civil and administrative tribunal, issued 640 – under the ambit of the Orwellian-named Open Courts Act.

Raw data doesn’t explain the reason for this. Maybe there are simply more applications of this type south of the Murray than in the rest of the nation, or quite possibly the judges in that jurisdiction are more predisposed to keeping proceedings and identities hidden.

Some of that tally would be reduced by subsequent court orders to lift the veil of secrecy – and that would also apply in all the other jurisdictions.

It was not entirely surprising that the accused in a high-profile Melbourne rape case managed to have his identity protected by a county court suppression order.

Quite apart from the case attracting attention in the media and elsewhere, the accused himself was also repeatedly described in news bulletins as a “well-connected Melbourne businessman”.

On Tuesday a jury found him guilty of two counts of rape and one of sexual assault of a former employee visiting his home. An intention to appeal has been flagged by his lawyers – in fact his defence counsel said that his client has been the subject of a “gross miscarriage of justice” and that there was a prospective application to stay the sentencing.

His psychiatrist has given evidence about his mental health. In 2024, after the high-profile individual was charged, she told the court that he had a series of inpatient admissions related to mental distress as a result of being charged and prospectively being identified in the media. A suicide attempt was self-reported.

She had been told by her patient: “If I’m guilty, put it on the front page.” Among many in Melbourne his identity is an open secret.

Clearly, there are balls in the air that are yet to land. Despite the verdict, the suppression order on his identity remains in place to be revisited in court on Monday, where his lawyers could apply to extend the order.

This could well be a situation where a person is clinging to their business and social standing, which already has been jettisoned.

The familiar shibboleth trotted out at judicial conferences is that justice is open, the courts have to be seen to be doing their work, otherwise who knows what monkey business judges might get up to.

summary.en: Everyone in Australia on 11 August, including international sports stars and musicians are expected to complete the Census.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
On Tuesday 11 August, Italian footballing history will be made as Juventus and Palermo FC face off in Perth as part of the Calcio Italiano tournament.

That same night, players will also partake in a distinctly Australian tradition — the Census of Population and Housing .

The survey is conducted by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) every five years. It's designed to capture and count every person in the country on Census night.

That includes international visitors, such as the Piedmont-based Juventus and the Sicilian-based Palermo football teams, who will be competing in the Australian pre-season football tournament for the first time.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Female footballers from Chelsea FC Women will also be in Australia ahead of the final match of the Sydney Super Cup on 12 August.

It's not just sports stars; English trip-hop collective Massive Attack are set to perform at Rod Laver Arena in Melbourne on Census night. German-French cellist Nicolas Altstaedt and French lutenist Thomas Dunford will be hosting a masterclass in Melbourne that same day.

United States actors Zac Efron, Kate Walsh, and supermodel Tyra Banks are among the international celebrities who have reportedly relocated to Australia in recent years. Meanwhile, Punjabi rapper and songwriter Karan Aujla is set to perform in Perth on 13 August.

SBS News has been unable to independently verify the whereabouts of any of these people on Census night. However, anyone in the country on 11 August is expected to complete the Census.

Liz Allen, a demographer at the Australian National University's Centre for Social Policy Research, said the Census is deliberately designed to provide a broad snapshot of the nation.

"It gives us an important reference point of who's in the country at that particular time," she told SBS News.

The Census is compulsory for all Australians, international visitors, temporary residents, migrants and refugees in the country . However, Australians who are overseas on 11 August do not complete the Census.

Allen said that allows the ABS to collect information on "who might be staying over at a friend's house or gran's house" on Census night.

"So it's not just a Census of people. It's a Census of Population and Housing. It gives us essential information on ... how and where we live and then housing stock in the country."

The Census is usually completed online; however, individual and paper forms can be requested if preferred.

For international visitors and students staying in hotels, motels or student accommodation, instructions on how to complete the Census will be provided by accommodation staff.

title.en: An issue of trust: The 'worrying' problem Australia faces
title.zh: 信任问题：澳大利亚面临的“令人担忧”的问题

summary.en: Australia has dropped to below pre-pandemic levels on a key social measure.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia celebrates the value of mateship, but distrust between the population has grown to the highest level reported this decade.

A survey of over 3,500 people, conducted by the Australian National University in June, suggests Australians trust each other less than they did during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Professor Nicholas Biddle, head of ANU's School of Politics and International Relations, said some of the findings were concerning.

"Worryingly, interpersonal trust among Australians has fallen to 5.32 on a scale of 0 to 10 — the lowest value recorded in ANUpoll during the 2020s,'' he said.

"This sits below the pre-COVID value of 5.53 recorded in October 2019 and reverses the increase in trust observed during the pandemic."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Researchers asked participants three questions: whether they believed most people could be trusted, whether someone would take advantage of them if given the chance, and whether people are generally helpful or selfish in their choices.

While the results for all three indicated declining trust, the most dramatic decrease was in belief that others can be trusted, Biddle said.

He also noted that trust remains strongest among "older Australians, degree holders and the employed".

The findings follow data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ General Social Survey from 2025 that found half of Australians felt others could be trusted — compared to 61 per cent in 2020.

Similarly, Scanlon Foundation Research Institute CEO Anthea Hancocks said the findings reflected those of her organisation.

"People who are employed each day or very often are going to a workplace where there are other people working towards a similar goal — and they're getting paid," she explained.

"That gives you a greater sense of self-worth that you may not necessarily have if you're unemployed."

She suggested that higher trust among older Australians may be related to her organisation's findings that this cohort had "a higher sense of belonging than any other age group".

"That's generally because they know the world in which they're living; they're quite comfortable with their circumstances," she said.

"They know what they are and have an understanding of what the future holds. Unlike young people, whose sense of belonging is way below average."

The ANUpoll also found that between March and June of 2026, life satisfaction in Australia plateaued at 6.22 out of 10.

Over the same period, the proportion of those who experienced difficult or very difficult levels of financial stress decreased slightly from 34.9 per cent in March to 33 per cent in June.

summary.en: AstraZeneca's Zoladex reversal has left some patients with more questions than answers.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Ashleigh Middleton has spent months campaigning to keep a drug that's holding her cancer at bay on Australian shelves.

Now she's won — but says the uncertainty surrounding long-term access hasn't gone away.

The 31-year-old breast cancer patient was shocked when it was announced in April that Zoladex — a monthly implant used to suppress hormones in women with hormone-positive breast cancer as well as a range of other conditions affecting women — would be pulled from the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) and no longer supplied through its usual distribution pathway from 1 November.

The decision, made by the drug's manufacturer, AstraZeneca, prompted concern among patients and clinicians who questioned how those who rely on the treatment would access an alternative and whether suitable substitutes would be available for all conditions the implant is used to treat.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Angered by the move and worried about the precedent it could set for other medications, Middleton started a change.org petition, calling on AstraZeneca to reverse the decision and urging the federal government and the Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee to secure PBS-listed alternatives.

The company now says it will provide the monthly implant free of charge to patients who have no suitable alternative, with no end date listed — a shift from its earlier plan to provide six months of free access while patients transitioned to other arrangements.

Asked whether AstraZeneca could guarantee the medication would remain available, a spokesperson told SBS News: "The Zoladex Continuity Program is not a time-bound program."

For Middleton, it's a win worth celebrating — but not one that has settled her nerves.

"It's a really, really good step in the right direction, but it's definitely not all the way there," she tells SBS News.

"But I think AstraZeneca have recognised it was probably a bad decision on their part, so at least putting a little something extra in there, saying it's indefinitely going to be available and that there's no cut-off time, I think is a positive," Middleton says.

Two weeks on from that announcement, with November fast approaching, those affected are left with a mix of celebration, confusion and ongoing concern about what access will look like in practice.

While many people may not have heard of Zoladex, its 3.6mg implant has become a lifeline for many of the patients who rely on it.

title.en: What is Garma Festival? Australia's biggest Indigenous gathering returns for 2026
title.zh: 什么是加尔马节？澳大利亚最大的原住民聚会将于2026年回归

summary.en: The annual Garma Festival, Australia's largest Indigenous gathering, is set to return this weekend on Yolŋu Country, celebrating Indigenous culture.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚最大的原住民聚会——一年一度的加尔马节将于本周末在约尔古地区举行，庆祝原住民文化。

body.en:
Thousands of people will travel to north-east Arnhem Land this week as the Garma Festival returns to Yolŋu Country for four days of ceremony, culture and national conversation.

Held on Gumatj Country in the Northern Territory, Garma remains Australia's largest Indigenous cultural gathering .

This year marks more than a quarter of a century since it started as a small community gathering, and will run from 31 July until 3 August.

Each year it brings together Yolŋu Elders, artists, young people, political leaders, academics, business representatives and visitors from across the country.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It is a place where ancient ceremony sits alongside some of Australia's biggest conversations about First Nations policy.

This year, those discussions will unfold without Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, despite his commitment last year to attend every Garma while serving as prime minister.

Hosted by the Yothu Yindi Foundation since 1999, Garma was established to celebrate and strengthen Yolŋu culture while creating a place where Aboriginal knowledge, leadership and ideas could be shared with the broader Australian community.

The word Garma comes from Yolŋu Matha and refers to a meeting place where different ideas come together through a process of two-way learning.

That philosophy remains central to the festival today. While Garma is grounded in Yolŋu ceremony and tradition, it has also become one of Australia's most influential forums for discussion on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander affairs.

Each year, governments, community organisations, academics and industry leaders travel to Arnhem Land to listen, learn and engage directly with Yolŋu leaders on Country.

Garma is held at Gulkula, a sacred ceremonial site on Gumatj Country near Nhulunbuy in north-east Arnhem Land.

Surrounded by stringybark forest and overlooking the Gulf of Carpentaria, Gulkula has been a place of ceremony and renewal for generations.

According to Yolŋu tradition, it is where the ancestor Ganbulapula introduced the yidaki into Yolŋu life, making it one of the region's most culturally significant places.

Unlike many conferences, Garma is held on Yolŋu Country and led on Yolŋu terms.

Rather than Aboriginal leaders travelling to Canberra, governments, institutions and organisations travel to Arnhem Land, placing First Nations culture, knowledge and authority at the centre of the national conversation.

Visitors camp on Country throughout the four-day festival and are asked to observe cultural protocols guided by their Yolŋu hosts.
